cards.title: Rethinking insurance distribution in Canada
cards.claim: Independent brokers write an estimated majority of Canadian P&C premium, mainly personal and small commercial, while digital and aggregator penetration remains low versus the UK and Europe.

stat.what: estimated broker share of Canadian P&C premium volumes

cards.relevance: Shows brokers are structurally central to Canadian personal lines, so channel mix differences are expected rather than anomalous.
cards.limit: Estimate without methodology; conflicts with the 58% figure from another source and contains no loss ratios.

cards.title: Insurance Brokers Association of Canada Broker Identity Program renewal (Wynward)
cards.claim: Brokers and independent agents hold a bit over half of Canadian P&C distribution while direct and online home channels grow faster.

stat.what: broker plus independent agent share of Canadian P&C distribution in 2025; online home channels growing 11% CAGR

cards.relevance: Gives a lower, more conservative market-share benchmark and signals direct channel competition for home.
cards.limit: Trade-press figures with unstated source; all P&C, not personal lines only.

cards.title: Smythe: state of the property and casualty brokerage
cards.claim: Brokerages earn base commissions that vary by line and insurer, plus contingent profit commissions that rise as the insurer's earned loss ratio on the broker's placed business falls.

stat.what: typical base commission range; contingent commission driven by earned loss ratio and volume

cards.relevance: Confirms that loss-ratio-linked contingents are standard in Canada and can be used to align B07 and other brokers with profitability.
cards.limit: Summary article; no profitability or contingent share-of-revenue figures in the excerpt.

cards.title: Travelers is paying agents more profit-sharing than it planned
cards.claim: Contingent payouts track the profitability of a producer's book, so lower loss ratios raise payouts and rising loss ratios would reduce them.

stat.what: Travelers personal insurance loss and LAE ratio, nine months 2026 vs prior year

cards.relevance: Illustrates the incentive mechanism and the cyclicality that could mask or reveal broker quality problems.
cards.limit: US carrier and brokers, not Canadian personal lines; cat-driven swings.

cards.title: Definity's growth is broker-led, and the insurer says more acquisitions could follow
cards.claim: A large Canadian insurer's personal lines premium surged mostly via brokers while direct grew slowly, and its auto combined ratio stayed in the mid-90s despite integration costs.

stat.what: personal lines GWP growth (mostly brokers) vs direct channel growth, Q2 2026; personal auto combined ratio 95.1%

cards.relevance: Peer example of broker-led rapid growth with auto results holding, alongside the growth-quality concern.
cards.limit: Growth largely from an acquired book, not new broker partnerships; no loss ratio by channel.

cards.title: Catastrophe losses push Definity to Q3 underwriting loss
cards.claim: Personal property results swung sharply worse on catastrophe losses, showing home loss ratios are volatile and weather-driven regardless of channel.

stat.what: personal property combined ratio Q3 2026 vs Q3 2025; cat losses added 32.6 points

cards.relevance: Challenges attributing weak broker Home loss ratio to broker risk quality; geography, cat exposure and mix may drive it.
cards.limit: Single insurer quarter; not split by channel.

cards.title: Co-operators' own captive insurer won't touch complex commercial risk without a broker
cards.claim: Even an agent-led insurer writes its complex and specialty risk exclusively through independent brokers, supporting the idea that brokers handle harder risks and channel mix explains some results.

stat.what: Co-operators General combined ratio Q2 2026 (not split by channel)

cards.relevance: Supports the counter-hypothesis that broker books skew toward complex risks, so raw loss ratios overstate broker risk quality problems.
cards.limit: Commercial focus; says nothing quantitative about personal lines broker vs agent loss ratios.

cards.title: Aviva Canada's combined ratio improves, but the commercial book is flashing a warning to brokers
cards.claim: A broker-distributed Canadian insurer improved its personal lines combined ratio while holding margin discipline and growing through brokers and partners.

stat.what: Aviva Canada personal lines combined ratio H1 2026, down 3.3 points

cards.relevance: Shows a broker-led personal lines book can be profitable, so the broker channel is not inherently worse.
cards.limit: Company-level, not channel-level; pricing and cat experience drove the improvement.

cards.title: Insurance Agent KPIs: producer performance dashboard playbook
cards.claim: A producer loss ratio consistently running well above the carrier average signals appetite drift or weak risk selection, and should be tracked alongside quote-to-bind, renewal and average policy size.

stat.what: producer loss ratio above carrier average flagged as a problem threshold

cards.relevance: Gives a practical trigger for a broker scorecard, applicable to B07 versus other brokers.
cards.limit: Vendor practitioner rule of thumb, not a regulatory or Canadian standard.

cards.title: Performing your agency report card (network loss ratio management)
cards.claim: When loss ratios stay high, carriers dig into individual agencies and new-business submissions may be limited or the appointment ended after a rehabilitation attempt.
cards.relevance: Describes a graduated escalation path from analysis to restriction to termination that could apply to B07.
cards.limit: Agency-network perspective from the US; anecdotal quotes rather than data.

cards.title: A.M. Best: Rapid premium growth warrants greater MGA oversight
cards.claim: Rapidly growing delegated distribution can lead partners to write unprofitable business to earn commissions, so carriers should do due diligence, align incentives and monitor performance.

stat.what: growth in US MGA-written direct premium in 2023 to $81.4 billion

cards.relevance: Direct analogue to new broker partnerships with delegated authority growing quickly.
cards.limit: US MGAs with underwriting authority, more extreme than ordinary brokers.

cards.title: How to mitigate adverse risk selection
cards.claim: Growth can bring underpriced, poorly fitting business that erodes margin gradually, and controls include appetite-aware prioritization and portfolio-level feedback loops.
cards.relevance: Frames the mechanism by which fast broker growth could degrade loss ratio and what controls help.
cards.limit: Vendor marketing content, not about Canadian personal lines or broker partnerships specifically.

cards.title: How fake brokers are exploiting Canada's hunt for cheaper car insurance
cards.claim: Unlicensed intermediaries alter application details such as driving experience or vehicle use, and recommended controls include licence verification through FSRA or the AMF and payment-channel checks.
cards.relevance: Links application misrepresentation to premium and claims leakage and offers verification controls for intermediary onboarding.
cards.limit: Qualitative with no prevalence statistics; focuses on unlicensed, not licensed, brokers.

cards.title: FSRA imposes $100,000 penalty on fake broker
cards.claim: Ontario's regulator penalized an individual for acting as an insurance agent without a valid licence, who did not contest the action.

stat.what: FSRA administrative penalty for unlicensed insurance activity

cards.relevance: Shows regulator enforcement exists and that licence checks on broker partners are material.
cards.limit: Single enforcement case; no data on frequency or impact on loss ratios.

cards.title: Insurance regulators release final guidance on fair treatment of customers
cards.claim: Canadian regulators issued principles-based joint guidance covering insurers and intermediaries including brokers and MGAs, with governance and outsourcing among its topics.
cards.relevance: Establishes that insurers carry conduct expectations tied to the intermediaries they use, relevant to oversight design.
cards.limit: News summary; does not detail insurer oversight duties, and the guidance is from 2018.

cards.title: The next frontier for sustainable growth: capturing the cost advantage of direct insurance
cards.claim: Direct insurers have much lower sales cost ratios than multichannel insurers, but aggregator-reliant direct players pay high commissions.
cards.relevance: Frames online channel economics versus broker commissions.
cards.limit: Only seen as a search snippet; page fetch timed out twice, so figures are unverified and not Canada-specific.
